Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
245 PM EDT Sun Aug 30 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 244 PM EDT Sunday...

No significant changes made with this forecast package.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 244 PM EDT Sunday...

1. Showers ending by midnight tonight with some patchy fog 
toward sunrise on Monday expected in favored areas. 

2. Several rounds of showers and thunderstorms possible Tuesday 
through Wednesday, but timing and placement of precipitation is very 
challenging. 

3. Trending drier late week and into the weekend with 
seasonably cool conditions. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 244 PM EDT Sunday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: GOES-19 Day Cloud Phase Distinction product shows 
extensive cloud cover acrs our cwa this aftn, with some breaks and 
better instability north of Montreal ahead of approaching cold 
front. These breaks have allowed temps to warm into the 70s with sfc 
based CAPE values around 1000 J/kg, but <300 J/kg over our cwa, due 
to the clouds and lack of sfc heating. As boundary drops southward 
toward the International Border by 00z, a broken line of showers 
with a few rumbles of thunder wl be possible near the border, but 
thunder threat should be quickly dissipating around sunset. Have 
lowered qpf amounts by 25 to 35% acrs the board, as precip amounts 
have been less with minimal instability today, as temps struggle to 
reach 70F. 

After fropa flow becomes north-northwest upslope with moisture 
trapped below developing/lowering subsidence inversion, which should 
allow for the development of low stratus type clouds, especially 
acrs the mtns. As subsidence inversion conts to lower toward morning 
and winds become light, thinking some patchy fog wl be possible acrs 
the trrn, favorable valley and areas that receive >0.10" of 
rainfall. Fog/low clouds wl slowly burn off by 10 AM Monday with 
increasing amounts of sunshine expected along with comfortable temps 
in the 70s.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Given the upcoming pattern the predictability of precip 
timing and placement is low, especially toward Weds/Weds night, as a 
large spread remains in latest guidance. Latest guidance indicates 
CAMs are much further north with axis of precip late Monday night 
into Tues, while larger scale guidance is mostly a miss to our 
south. Given the latest trends have cutback on pops Monday 
night/Tues morning and continued to show highest values south of a 
MSS to BTV to LEB line. Feel most of the precip remains south of our 
cwa thru 12z Tues, given the position of 1024mb sfc high pres nosing 
into the northern cwa with a developing sharp sw (1.40") to ne 
(0.45") pw gradient acrs our cwa. Furthermore, highest instability 
parameters, including elevated CAPE values stay mostly south of the 
NY State Thruway as northwest flow btwn 700-500mb keeps us on the 
cooler side of the boundary into Tues. Given these factors have 
trimmed back qpf and pops for Monday night into Tues, with highest 
chc/low likely near our cwa border with WFO ALY/BUF. Much lower 
values acrs the NEK of VT. 

By Weds potent closed 850 to 500mb cyclonic circulation is progged 
to be north of the Great Lakes, with departing ridge acrs the north 
Atlantic. This wl increase the pres gradient acrs our cwa, with 
increasing winds likely, along with better chcs for showers and 
thunderstorms, especially on Weds aftn/evening. Height field 
analysis would suggest strong mid lvl flow btwn low pres to the 
north and high pres to the south, question wl be magnitude of 
instability and timing of best sfc convergence. For now have 
continued with NBM for pops with mention of showers and storms, but 
potential for a few strong/severe wl need to be watched.

KEY MESSAGE 3: An upper level low will remain around heading through 
the end of the week, so there will be the chance of a few showers 
each day, particularly in the afternoon due to diurnal heating. 
However, most of the time it will be dry. Heading into the weekend, 
the upper low will continue to push east and surface high pressure 
will build south out of Canada, causing conditions to trend drier. 
However, there is uncertainty among the ensembles for when the low 
moves out and when it becomes completely dry. Currently, 
probabilities of precipitation during the day are between 10-30 
percent, mostly driven off EPS members. However, even if these 
wetter solutions verify, the greatest extent of rain would be some 
isolated to scattered showers. Highs should be in the 60s and 70s 
and lows should be in the 40s and 50s.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z SUNDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Through 18Z Monday...Prevailing VFR conditions are expected to
continue at all terminals through the next 18 hours. A cold front
will sink south from Quebec with showers already across northern New
York and portions of northern Vermont. Shower chances and 
confidence of rain over northern terminals including 
MSS/EFK/BTV/SLK/PBG will increase by 18Z with perhaps some brief
heavier downpours that could lead to MVFR vsbys reductions. A 
few isolated thunderstorms will also be possible between 18Z-22Z
in the vicinity of the aforementioned terminals, but confidence
in terminal thunderstorms are low at this time, and thus have
not included thunder in any TAF lines. Should a thunderstorm 
pass over a terminal, MVFR/IFR vsbys will be possible with 
changeable winds. Have generally only used PROB30 for rain 
shower vsby reductions this afternoon at this time. Winds around
10-15 knots will shift from the south to the southwest this 
morning and then west throughout the day as the cold front moves
south. A few gusts around 15-20 MPH will be possible as the 
front passes through each terminal, mainly at MSS/BTV. Showers 
will taper off towards 00Z, with increasing confidence in patchy
fog at the climo favored terminals closer to 06Z tonight. 
Should any terminal receive rain, especially if close to 22- 
00Z, fog chances will increase.

Outlook...

Monday Night: VFR. Chance SHRA.
Tuesday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Likely SHRA,
Slight chance TSRA.
Tuesday Night: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Wednesday: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Likely SHRA,
Chance TSRA.
Wednesday Night: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Likely
SHRA, Slight chance TSRA.
Thursday: MVFR/IFR conditions possible. Chance SHRA.
Thursday Night: Mainly VFR, with local IFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Friday: Mainly MVFR, with areas IFR possible. Chance SHRA, Slight
chance TSRA.
